key_insight: GenFish ranks potential protein targets for molecules using generative retrieval without treating unmeasured molecule–protein pairs as negatives.
clinical_relevance: This approach could support target discovery and drug repurposing, including oncology research, but the abstract reports no cancer-specific or clinical validation.
method: Convert frozen protein language-model features into shared semantic identifiers using residual vector quantization.
Predict identifier sequences autoregressively from molecular fingerprints.
Rank proteins by identifier likelihood across a human-protein catalogue.
evidence_signal: On ProTargetBench, covering 20,431 reviewed human proteins, GenFish achieved higher mean performance on all three full-catalogue retrieval metrics than seven baselines across 198 held-out molecules.
watch_item: Evaluation relies on incomplete recorded bioactivity; predicted targets require experimental validation.
paper_title: Generative Retrieval for Reverse Target Fishing with a Proteome-Scale Benchmark
